resources.string:
The Minsk Military Cemetery on Kozlova Street is one of the oldest and most significant memorial sites in the capital of Belarus. It was founded at the end of the 19th century, roughly in the 1870s–1880s, and was originally intended for servicemen who died on duty and for veterans of various wars.

 Participants of the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–1878, the First World War, the Civil War and the Great Patriotic War rest here. Partisans, officers, Heroes of the Soviet Union and well-known figures of the Soviet era are also buried here. The Minsk Military Cemetery has become a kind of chronicle of the military history of Belarus, reflecting the fates and deeds of people who defended their homeland in different historical periods.

 The mass grave of Soviet soldiers who fell during the Great Patriotic War draws particular attention. Memorials, obelisks and neat headstones with military symbols give the cemetery a solemn and austere feel. It often becomes the center of commemorative events, especially on Victory Day and other days of military glory.

 Architecturally, the cemetery is a well-kept area with alleys, conifers and old headstones, many of which date back to before the revolution. Some slabs still bear inscriptions in pre-reform Russian spelling, which gives the place a special historical atmosphere.

 Despite being close to the city center and busy streets, it is quiet and respectfully calm here. The Minsk Military Cemetery on Kozlova is not just a burial ground but an important cultural and historical monument, a reminder of the price of peace and the courage of those who defended it.

How to add a burial place?
Check the result on the Map tab: the new marker should be in its place.
If the Save button is disabled, the full name is empty or a date is invalid: such a field is highlighted in red.
The numbers on the map and the route line follow the order of the stops; the preview is shown right in the editor.
Check the text before recording: stresses in surnames, years written out in words, abbreviations spelled out in full.
The author will see your reply under More → My requests.
Deleted items can only be restored by hand, so make sure the right card is open before deleting.

string-array.name: burial_place_steps
string-array.item: Admin → Burial places → “Add place”.
Choose the type: grave, mass grave or monument.
Enter the section, row and plot from the cemetery plate. This is more accurate than GPS, and visitors search by these numbers.
Stand by the grave and tap “My location”. If the marker is off, tap the map at the right point.
Add a photo and a short description if you have them, and tap “Save”.

string-array.name: veteran_steps
string-array.item: Admin → Veterans → “Add veteran”. The app assigns the card number itself.
Full name and years of life as on the plate, for example “1905–1966”.
The category sets the filter in the list and on the map: “Heroes of the Soviet Union” or “Artists”.
Pick the dates of birth and death in the calendar: the “On this day” section and favorite reminders rely on them.
Choose the burial place from the list of places created in advance.
Add a portrait: the face in the center, the app compresses the photo itself.
Awards are set with plus and minus: two Orders of the Red Star means “2” next to the order.
Build the biography from paragraphs and captioned photos. Arrows change the order, the cross removes a block.
Use the language switch at the top of the form to fill in translations: empty fields show the Russian text.

string-array.name: tour_steps
string-array.item: Admin → Tours → “Add tour”.
Give it a title and a short description, for example “Heroes of the Soviet Union, 40 minutes”.
Tap “Add stop” and find the place by surname, section number or type.
For each stop write the text the visitor reads at the grave and attach an audio guide.
Set the order of the stops with the arrows.

string-array.name: voice_over_steps
string-array.item: A biography lasts 1–3 minutes, a tour stop 30–90 seconds.
mp3 or m4a format, file size up to 50 MB.
ElevenLabs or Yandex SpeechKit work for speech synthesis. A live voice recorded in a quiet room often sounds better.
Send the file to your phone and upload it with “Add audio” in the veteran\'s card or in the stop.

string-array.name: requests_steps
string-array.item: “Moderation” holds materials from relatives. Fix the text, remove extra photos and tap “Approve”: everything goes to the card at once, captioned “From the family archive”.
“Feedback” holds visitors\' messages and error reports. Mark a message as reviewed and write a reply if you like.
The app filters obscene texts and indecent photos before sending, but this check can be bypassed, so review everything before approving.

string-array.name: add_administrator_steps
string-array.item: The new administrator signs in to the app once: with Google in More or via “Administrator sign-in” with their e-mail.
A super administrator opens Admin → “Administrators” and adds them by e-mail.
Storage → Rules: add the new administrator\'s UID (it can be copied on the Administrators screen) to the isAdmin() function list and tap “Publish”. Without this they cannot upload photos and audio.
After restarting the app, the new administrator gets the Admin tab.
To revoke rights, remove the administrator on the Administrators screen and delete their UID from the Storage rules.
Super administrators are assigned only in the Firebase Console: the OurMemory/SuperAdmins node, the UID key with the value true (and the same UID in OurMemory/Admins).

string-array.name: troubleshooting_steps
string-array.item: A photo or audio doesn\'t upload — check the internet and the file size. If the error repeats, ask the developer to add your UID to the Storage rules.
“No administrator rights” on sign-in — the database has no record with your UID in OurMemory/Admins. Follow the steps in the Administrators section.
A visitor doesn\'t see the changes — the app loads data once per launch, new content appears after a restart.
An administrator sign-in on a visitor\'s phone resets their Google sign-in. Work from your own phone.
